lookAtThis.title: Venue of the Month
lookAtThis.summary: Hosting all sorts of live music in the heart of Belfast's gay district.
lookAtThis.content: Tucked right in the beating heart of Belfast's gay district, The Reporter Bar is where good tunes, good drinks, and good people collide — usually with a band blasting the roof off for good measure. More than just a bar, it's a space where local music gets a proper platform with no pretence, no industry nonsense, just real bands and real punters. From indie and punk to drag cabaret and DJ nights that run till the small hours, The Reporter is serving up a proper slice of Belfast nightlife. It's inclusive, it's community ran, and it's the kind of place where you can end up best mates with the band and the bar staff by the end of the night. Whether you're there to dance, drink, or just take in the chaos. The Reporter always top of our report!
lookAtThis.author: Jonny Moore

lookAtThis.title: Looking back at TradFest
lookAtThis.summary: Bigger than ever, TradFest wasn't just a hit, it smashed it clean out of the park!
lookAtThis.content: If you missed TradFest this year, we're not mad… just extremely disappointed in you. Because honestly? That. Was. Class. Bigger than ever, with fiddles flying, bodhráns banging, and more foot stomping than a ceilí at a wedding with an open bar, TradFest 2025 showed us all that trad isn't just alive — it's thriving. From the streets of the Cathedral Quater to late night sessions in tiny pubs where the walls practically sweat Guinness, the atmosphere was unreal. And the lineup? Class. A mix of old masters and new-school trad-fusion heads proved the genre's not stuck in the past, it's blazing forward with its roots firmly planted. Call it trad, folk, or just straight-up soul music — whatever it was, it rocked. Same time next year? I'll see ye there.
lookAtThis.author: Jonny Moore

lookAtThis.title: Féile an Phobail 2025
lookAtThis.summary: Ireland's biggest community arts festival is nearly here, read more for all the craic.
lookAtThis.content: August in Belfast means only one thing. Féile an Phobail! Yes, it's nearly upon us, and it's looking bigger, bolder and buzzier than ever. What started as a West Belfast community response to censorship and negativity during the Troubles has grown into a full-blown celebration of arts, culture, music and straight up good craic! Féile 2025 is promising hundreds of events across music, comedy, talks, theatre and more with something for everyone! (Even your wee granny!) Expect performances from local legends, international guests, political heavyweights, grassroots voices, and maybe even your wee neighbour from up the road who's finally taking their one-man show public. Whether you're into trad, hip hop, spoken word or just showing up for the vibes, Féile's got you covered. Make sure and check out the programme good and early and get the day booked off, and for the love of all things Belfast, get stuck in!
lookAtThis.author: Jonny Moore

lookAtThis.title: Legends Never Die
lookAtThis.summary: The Prince of Darkness may be gone but he leaves behind one hell of a legacy.
lookAtThis.content: If you've ever headbanged in your bedroom, screamed along to something spooky, or worn eyeliner you absolutely couldn't pull off, chances are you owe something to the Prince of Darkness. While the sad news of his passing hit hard, it's not the end. Far from it. What this legend leaves behind is more than just albums and outrageous stage sets. It's a whole movement, a whole generation of music misfits, and the unapologetic belief that being weird, loud, and real is something to be proud of. From basement gigs to arena blowouts, the ripple effect of his sound and spirit lives on. Whether you worshipped him or just nodded along respectfully, it's safe to say he changed the game. Legends like this don't really die. They just get louder in the background.
lookAtThis.author: Jonny Moore

whatsHappenin.title: Féile Trad Trail brings the craic back into the city centre.
whatsHappenin.summary: Trad tunes, good pints, and proper Belfast energy taking over the town.
whatsHappenin.content: What's better than a trad session in a packed pub? How about a whole trail of them, winding through the city centre, led by some of the best local talent around? The Féile Trad Trail is back and it's pure magic — from lunchtime lilt to late-night toe-tapping. You'll find fiddles, flutes and fierce harmonies lighting up venues all across Belfast. It's a celebration of Irish music and the kind of craic you can only get when the Guinness is flowing. Bring your mates, follow the tunes, and don't be afraid to belt your heart out!
whatsHappenin.author: Jonny Moore

whatsHappenin.title: There. Will. Be. BLOOD!
whatsHappenin.summary: Revenge of the Hot Ghoul Summer. Spooky beats, queer chaos, and full-on drag mayhem.
whatsHappenin.content: The Black Box is about to get bloody — and we mean that in the best way possible. Hot Ghoul Summer is back from the grave with a vengeance, serving up a night of spooky queer joy, killer performances, and dancefloor chaos. Expect drag, DJs, sweat, sequins, and maybe even a séance. It's part club night, part cabaret, all filth. Dress to slay and don't come expecting subtlety! This is full-throttle, scream-if-you-want-to-go-faster, camp-as-hell energy. Bring your inner ghoul and leave your shame at the door.
whatsHappenin.author: Jonny Moore

whatsHappenin.title: Pour Out Your Heart - Your Guide to Local Open Mic Nights.
whatsHappenin.summary: From heartfelt ballads to weird poetry. Here's where to grab the mic in Belfast.
whatsHappenin.content: Think you've got a song in your heart or a poem in your pocket? Belfast's open mic scene is calling. Whether you're a first-timer with shaky hands or a seasoned strummer ready to steal the show, there's a space for you in bars and cafés across the city. We'll keep you updated as the main venues, Voodoo, Lavery's, Maverick and the Reporter rework their summer schedules!
whatsHappenin.author: Jonny Moore

whatsHappenin.title: Tributes, Get Your Tributes
whatsHappenin.summary: A guide to Belfast's tribute acts — just like the real thing, only with cheaper pints.
whatsHappenin.content: Counldn't afford Springsteen tickets? Missed your chance to see Bowie live? Fear not — Belfast's tribute scene is keeping the legends alive, one sweaty cover at a time. From spooky-accurate Queen acts to ABBA singalongs, Nirvana nostalgia and Taylor Swift nights that could fool your ma, these bands bring the big vibes without the big prices. Whether you're in it for the music, the mayhem or just a bit of shameless dancing, tribute gigs are where it's at. Bonus points if the lead singer actually looks the part.
whatsHappenin.author: Jonny Moore

whatsHappenin.title: Belfast Mela to Bring the Colour
whatsHappenin.summary: A riot of colour, culture, and community is landing in Botanic Gardens.
whatsHappenin.content: If there's one event that proves Belfast has well and truly opened its arms to the world, it's the Mela. Every year, Botanic Gardens explodes into a day-long celebration of global culture, music, dance, food, fashion, and vibes from every corner of the earth. Expect bhangra beats, African drumming, street food from about 12 continents (don't ask), and colour everywhere you look. Whether you're there for the music, the flavours, the family fun or just the craic, Belfast Mela is a proper celebration of what makes this city sing. Come hungry, leave smiling.
whatsHappenin.author: Jonny Moore
